description: Per-film actor counts and every average are taken only over films that have at least one row in film_actor.

a.request: Count the actors of each film, using only films that have at least one row in `film_actor` (films with no actor rows are left out entirely). Take the average of those counts, ignoring missing values. Keep the films with strictly more actors than that average and note how far each is above it. Among those films, average their actor counts again, ignoring missing values. Keep only the films strictly above this second average and note how far each is above it. If either average is missing, keep no films. Return one row: the sum of the remaining films' actor counts, the average of their excess over the first average, and the average of their excess over the second average, all ignoring missing values and unrounded.
a.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT film_id, COUNT(actor_id) AS cnt FROM film_actor GROUP BY film_id), a1 AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg1 FROM c), s1 AS (SELECT c.film_id, c.cnt, c.cnt - a1.avg1 AS ex1 FROM c CROSS JOIN a1 WHERE a1.avg1 IS NOT NULL AND c.cnt > a1.avg1), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg2 FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.film_id, s1.cnt, s1.ex1, s1.cnt - a2.avg2 AS ex2 FROM s1 CROSS JOIN a2 WHERE a2.avg2 IS NOT NULL AND s1.cnt > a2.avg2) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_actor_count, AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first, AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_second FROM s2

b.request: Considering only films with at least one film_actor row, compute each film's actor count and the average of those counts. Keep films whose count is strictly above that average, then average the kept films' counts. Keep only those strictly above this second average. Return one row with the total actor count of the remaining films, their average excess over the first average, and their average excess over the second average (nulls ignored, no rounding). If either average is missing, no films are kept
b.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT film_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM film_actor GROUP BY film_id), a1 AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg1 FROM c), k1 AS (SELECT c.film_id, c.cnt, a1.avg1 FROM c CROSS JOIN a1 WHERE c.cnt > a1.avg1), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg2 FROM k1), k2 AS (SELECT k1.film_id, k1.cnt, k1.avg1, a2.avg2 FROM k1 CROSS JOIN a2 WHERE k1.cnt > a2.avg2) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_actor_count, AVG(cnt - avg1) AS avg_excess_first, AVG(cnt - avg2) AS avg_excess_second FROM k2

c.request: How many actors does each film have, and what is the average of those counts (ignoring missing values)? Keep the films with strictly more actors than that average and note how far above it each one is. Among those films, average their actor counts again, keep only the ones strictly above that, and note how far above it they are too. If either average is missing, keep no films. Give me one row: the total actor count of the films that are left, their average excess over the first average, and their average excess over the second average, ignoring missing values and without rounding. Per-film actor counts and every average are taken only over films that have at least one row in film_actor.
c.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT film_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM film_actor GROUP BY film_id), a1 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg1 FROM c), s1 AS (SELECT c.film_id, c.n, a1.avg1 FROM c CROSS JOIN a1 WHERE c.n > a1.avg1), a2 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS avg2 FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.film_id, s1.n, s1.avg1, a2.avg2 FROM s1 CROSS JOIN a2 WHERE s1.n > a2.avg2) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_actor_count, AVG(n - avg1) AS avg_excess_over_first, AVG(n - avg2) AS avg_excess_over_second FROM s2

d.request: Per-film actor counts and every average (the first average and the second average over the films above it) are computed only over films that have at least one row in film_actor. For each such film, count its actors, then take the average of those counts, ignoring missing values. Keep the films with strictly more actors than that average and note how far above it each one is. Among those films, average their actor counts again, keep only the ones strictly above that second average, and note how far above it each one is. If either average is missing, keep no films. Give one row: the total actor count of the films that are left, their average excess over the first average, and their average excess over the second average, ignoring missing values and without rounding.
d.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT film_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM film_actor GROUP BY film_id), avg1 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS a1 FROM counts), above1 AS (SELECT c.film_id, c.n, c.n - a.a1 AS ex1 FROM counts c JOIN avg1 a ON 1=1 WHERE a.a1 IS NOT NULL AND c.n > a.a1), avg2 AS (SELECT AVG(n) AS a2 FROM above1), above2 AS (SELECT b.film_id, b.n, b.ex1, b.n - a.a2 AS ex2 FROM above1 b JOIN avg2 a ON 1=1 WHERE a.a2 IS NOT NULL AND b.n > a.a2) SELECT SUM(n) AS total_actor_count, AVG(ex1) AS avg_excess_over_first, AVG(ex2) AS avg_excess_over_second FROM above2
